name: Osaka · Kyoto
notes: Geometry and station positions © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL (route relations fetched via Overpass, simplified ~18 m), clipped to lng 134.9-136.1 / lat 34.3-35.15 (Akashi to Ōmi-Hachiman, Kansai Airport to Kurama; lines are truncated at that box). All lines are curated in scripts/kansai/lines.mjs (one all-stations OSM relation per line). Interchanges are merged when stations share a Japanese name within ~450 m, ignoring operator prefixes (山陽明石 = 明石, 京阪山科 = 山科); Osaka/Umeda (JR Osaka, Hankyu/Hanshin Osaka-umeda, Midōsuji Umeda), Namba (Nankai and Osaka Metro Namba, Kintetsu/Hanshin Osaka-Namba), Tennōji (with Kintetsu Ōsaka-Abenobashi and Hankai Tennōji-ekimae) and Sannomiya are one station each. Differently named transfer stations stay separate (Higashi-Umeda, Nishi-Umeda, Kitashinchi; JR Namba; Sannomiya-Hanadokeimae; Karasuma / Shijō; Kawaramachi / Gion-shijō). Segment years are first-opening years of each section, rounded; line colours are official where known, otherwise approximate (JR West, Hankyu, Hanshin, Keihan, Kintetsu, Nankai and the smaller operators). Station codes come from OSM refs (about a third of stations have none). Projects: Naniwasuji Line (construction, spring 2031), Osaka Monorail Kadoma-shi – Uryūdō (construction, FY2033), Hokuriku Shinkansen Kyoto (Katsuragawa) – Shin-Osaka (planned, no year) and Chūō Shinkansen Nara – Shin-Osaka (planned, nominal 2037); Hankyu Naniwasuji / Shin-Osaka links, Hankyu Osaka Airport Line, Imazatosuji, Kyoto Tōzai and Keihanna extensions (planned: listed in council report No. 8 of 2004, mostly dormant); JR Yumesaki Line to Yumeshima and Keihan Nakanoshima – Kujō (proposed). Their new stations are approximate (approx) and names provisional. OSM caveat (Nov 2026): several Keihan, JR and Kintetsu route relations were deleted from live OSM; they come from an older mirror snapshot or are rebuilt from track relations (see research/kansai.md). Not included: Kintetsu Yoshino Line, JR Kansai Main Line east of Kamo, Sagano Scenic Railway, cable cars and ropeways, limited-express-only services.

lines.name: Osaka Loop Line
lines.description: Loop through Osaka/Umeda, Kyōbashi, Tsuruhashi, Tennōji and Nishikujō. Closed into a loop in 1961, fully elevated 1964.

lines.description: Tōkaidō Main Line Osaka – Kobe (1874) and San'yō Main Line beyond Kobe (1888), clipped at the map box west of Nishi-Akashi.

lines.name: Wadamisaki Line
lines.description: San'yō Main Line branch Hyōgo – Wadamisaki (2.7 km, trains at peak hours only). No OSM route relation: drawn as a straight line between the two stations.

lines.description: Underground link Kyōbashi – Kitashinchi – Amagasaki, through-running with the Gakkentoshi and Takarazuka/Kobe lines.

lines.name: Kusatsu Line

lines.name: Naniwasuji Line
lines.description: New 7.2 km underground line built by Kansai Rapid Railway (third sector) and run by JR West and Nankai: Osaka (Umekita) – Nakanoshima – Nishi-Honmachi, then a JR branch to JR Namba and a Nankai branch to Shin-Imamiya via a new Nankai Shin-Namba station. Under construction since 2021; official opening spring 2031 (end of FY2030), kept at the 2026-08 cost review (¥642.5 bn). Intermediate station names are provisional and their positions approximate. No line colour yet (colour chosen for the map).

segments.label: JR branch: Osaka – JR Namba (target spring 2031)
Nankai branch: Nishi-Honmachi – Nankai Shin-Namba – Shin-Imamiya (target spring 2031)

lines.name: Tōkaidō Shinkansen
lines.description: JR Central, Tokyo – Shin-Osaka; only Kyoto – Shin-Osaka is inside the map box.

lines.name: San'yō Shinkansen
lines.description: JR West, Shin-Osaka – Hakata; Shin-Osaka – Nishi-Akashi inside the map box.

lines.name: Hokuriku Shinkansen (Tsuruga – Shin-Osaka)
lines.nameLocal: 北陸新幹線（敦賀・新大阪間）
lines.description: Planned extension from Tsuruga via Obama and Kyoto to Shin-Osaka, almost all in tunnel. In the 1973 整備計画, route fixed 2016–17; on 2026-07-15 the ruling parties chose the "Katsuragawa plan": a deep underground Kyoto station near JR Katsuragawa, ~5 km southwest of Kyoto Station. Construction not approved, environmental assessment unfinished; no official year (about 26 years of works, press expects the 2050s). Station sites approximate; the line continues north of the map toward Obama.

segments.label: Kyoto (Katsuragawa) – Matsuiyamate – Shin-Osaka (planned; no official year)

lines.name: Chūō Shinkansen (Nagoya – Osaka)
lines.nameLocal: リニア中央新幹線（名古屋・大阪間）
lines.description: SCMaglev, Nagoya – Nara area – Shin-Osaka. 整備計画 2011; environmental assessment started 2023-12, first assessment document not yet published (2026-07). The government's official aim is full opening "as early as 2037" (Cabinet policy 2025); JR Central has no Osaka date and Shinagawa – Nagoya itself is delayed past 2034, so the year is nominal. The Nara station site is undetermined (shown approximately) and the Osaka terminal position is not fixed.

segments.label: Nara area – Shin-Osaka (planned; government target "as early as 2037", nominal)

lines.name: Midōsuji Line
lines.description: Osaka's first subway (Umeda – Shinsaibashi, 1933). Through-running north of Esaka onto Kita-Osaka Kyuko to Minoh-Kayano.

lines.name: Kita-Osaka Kyuko (Namboku Line)
lines.nameLocal: 北大阪急行電鉄南北線
lines.description: Separate company, through-running with the Midōsuji Line. Senri-Chūō – Minoh-Kayano extension opened 2024-03-23.

lines.name: Chūō Line
lines.description: Nagata – Yumeshima; through-running with the Kintetsu Keihanna Line. Cosmosquare – Yumeshima opened 2025-01-19 for Expo 2025.

lines.name: Sakaisuji Line
lines.description: Tenjimbashisuji 6-chōme – Tengachaya; through-running with the Hankyu Senri and Kyoto lines.

lines.name: Imazatosuji Line
lines.description: Itakano – Imazato (2006). The southern extension to Yuzato-rokuchōme (6.7 km) is listed in the Kinki Regional Transport Council report No. 8 (2004) but has no business plan; Osaka City has run the "Imazato Liner" BRT trial on the corridor since 2019 (extended again from 2026-04).

segments.label: Imazato – Yuzato-rokuchōme extension (答申第8号 2004; BRT trial instead; no year; intermediate stations not published)

lines.name: Nankō Port Town Line (New Tram)
lines.nameLocal: 南港ポートタウン線（ニュートラム）

lines.name: Karasuma Line
lines.description: Kokusaikaikan – Takeda; through-running with the Kintetsu Kyoto Line.

lines.name: Tōzai Line
lines.description: Rokujizō – Uzumasa-Tenjingawa; Keihan Keishin Line trains run in from Misasagi. The western extension to Rakusai New Town (7.7 km) is in council report No. 8 (2004) and was a city "planned line" in 2006–07, frozen since for financial reasons.

segments.label: Uzumasa-Tenjingawa – Rakusai extension (答申第8号 2004; frozen; no year; intermediate stations not shown)

lines.name: Seishin-Yamate Line
lines.description: Seishin-chūō – Shin-Kōbe, through-running north onto the Hokushin Line (ex-Hokushin Kyuko, municipal since 2020-06-01) to Tanigami.

segments.label: Hokushin Line (Hokushin Kyuko 1988; Kobe City since 2020-06-01)

lines.name: Hankyu Kobe Line
lines.description: Osaka-umeda – Kobe-sannomiya, continuing over the Kobe Kōsoku Line to Shinkaichi.

lines.name: Hankyu Naniwasuji / Shin-Osaka links
lines.nameLocal: 阪急なにわ筋連絡線・新大阪連絡線
lines.description: Underground standard-gauge links planned by Hankyu: Osaka (Umekita, Naniwasuji Line) – Jūsō – Shin-Osaka, for through running to Kansai Airport. In council report No. 8 (2004) and the 2017 five-party agreement; MLIT's 2018 study rated them viable. No permit application or environmental assessment; Hankyu said in 2026-05 that nothing can proceed until the Hokuriku Shinkansen's Shin-Osaka station is fixed. No official year. (Hankyu still holds a dormant 1961 licence for an older elevated Jūsō – Shin-Osaka scheme.)

segments.label: Naniwasuji link: Osaka (Umekita) – Jūsō (~2.5 km; no year)
Shin-Osaka link: Jūsō – Shin-Osaka (~2.3 km; no year)

lines.name: Hankyu Osaka Airport Line
lines.description: Concept for a ~3–4 km underground branch from Sone (Takarazuka Line) to Osaka (Itami) Airport. Listed among medium/long-term lines in council report No. 8 (2004); MLIT's 2018 study judged it unprofitable and nothing has moved since (dormant). No year.

segments.label: Sone – Osaka Airport (答申第8号; dormant; no year)

lines.name: Hanshin Main Line
lines.description: Osaka-umeda – Motomachi, continuing over the Kobe Kōsoku Line to Nishidai (through-running onto the Sanyo Main Line).

lines.name: Keihan Main Line
lines.description: Yodoyabashi – Sanjō (Main Line) – Demachiyanagi (Ōtō Line, 1989).

lines.name: Keihan Nakanoshima Line
lines.description: Nakanoshima – Temmabashi (2008). Westward extension to Kujō (~2.1 km, toward Yumeshima): proposed. Osaka's 2025-08 study rated it the best option together with the JR Yumesaki Line extension; Keihan's 2026-05 plan still lists it as under study (construction from 2030 at the earliest). No official year.

segments.label: Nakanoshima – Kujō extension (~2.1 km; under study, no year)

lines.name: Keihan Keishin Line
lines.description: Misasagi – Biwako-hamaōtsu (partly street-running); trains continue over the Kyoto Tōzai Line to Uzumasa-Tenjingawa.

lines.name: Kintetsu Nara Line
lines.description: Osaka-Namba – Ōsaka-Uehommachi (Namba Line, 1970) – Fuse (Ōsaka Line tracks) – Kintetsu-Nara (1914). Through-running with the Hanshin Namba Line.

lines.name: Kintetsu Ōsaka Line
lines.description: Ōsaka-Uehommachi – Ise-Nakagawa, clipped at the map box.

segments.label: Yamato-Yagi – Nabari (1929–1930), clipped at the map box

lines.name: Kintetsu Kyoto Line
lines.description: Kyoto – Yamato-Saidaiji (Nara Electric Railway 1928); through-running with the Karasuma Line.

lines.name: Kintetsu Keihanna Line
lines.description: Nagata – Gakken-Nara-Tomigaoka, third-rail, through-running with the Osaka Metro Chūō Line to Yumeshima. Extension to Takanohara (3.8 km; alternative to Shin-Hōsono) is in council report No. 8 (2004) but frozen.

segments.label: Gakken-Nara-Tomigaoka – Takanohara extension (答申第8号 2004; frozen; no year)

lines.name: Nankai Main Line
lines.description: Namba – Wakayamashi (Hankai Railway 1885), clipped at the map box.

lines.name: Nankai Kōya Line
lines.description: Trains start at Namba over the Main Line; the Kōya Line proper starts at Shiomibashi/Kishinosato-Tamade. Clipped at the map box.

segments.label: Kōya Railway (Sakai-higashi – Nagano 1898); Namba trains via the Main Line

lines.name: Semboku Line
lines.description: Nakamozu – Izumi-Chūō (Semboku Rapid Railway 1971–1995; merged into Nankai 2025-04-01).

lines.name: Sanyo Main Line
lines.description: Nishidai – Sanyo-Himeji (Hyōgo – Suma 1910), clipped at the map box.

lines.name: Osaka Monorail Main Line
lines.description: Osaka Airport – Kadoma-shi (1990–1997). Southern extension Kadoma-shi – Uryūdō (~8.9 km, 5 new stations, provisional names): under construction since 2020, opening moved from 2029 to FY2033 (soft ground at Uryūdō). New station positions approximate.
